subject: chemistry
title: Significant figures, units and the data book

scenes.heading: Significant figures, units and the data book
scenes.sub: Stop losing easy marks on every calculation
scenes.say: Every measurement has a number, a unit and a level of certainty. Get these habits right now, and you'll stop losing easy marks for the rest of V C E.
scenes.caption: Every measurement has a number, a unit and a level of certainty. Get these habits right now, and you'll stop losing easy marks for the rest of VCE.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Blowing up a blurry photo can't add detail
scenes.science: Extra digits can't add precision a measurement never had
scenes.breaks: exact numbers, like 5 counted test tubes or 1000 mL in 1 L, have unlimited significant figures.
scenes.say: A photo from an old phone only has so much detail. Blow it up to poster size and it's just a bigger blurry picture. Significant figures are the digits your instrument actually captured. Writing twelve point three seven grams as twelve point three seven zero zero zero zero claims a precision that isn't there.
scenes.caption: A photo from an old phone only has so much detail. Blow it up to poster size and it's just a bigger blurry picture. Significant figures are the digits your instrument actually captured. Writing 12.37 g as 12.370000 g claims a precision that isn't there.

scenes.heading: Counting sig figs
points: Trailing zeros after a decimal count: 2.500
scenes.say: Non-zero digits always count. Zeros sandwiched between them count too. Leading zeros are just placeholders, like empty seats before the show starts, so they never count. Trailing zeros after a decimal point do count.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: How many significant figures are in 0.00450 g and in 6.020 × 10²³?
scenes.say: How many sig figs in zero point zero zero four five zero? The leading zeros don't count, but the trailing zero does, so three. In six point zero two zero times ten to the twenty-three, only count the first part: four sig figs.
scenes.caption: How many sig figs in 0.00450? The leading zeros don't count, but the trailing zero does, so 3. In 6.020 × 10²³, only count the first part: 4 sig figs.

scenes.heading: Two different rules
scenes.say: Times and divide, count the digits. Add and subtract, count the decimals. Two point five times three point one four two gives seven point nine, two sig figs. One oh five point two plus zero point three four six gives one oh five point five, one decimal place.
scenes.caption: Times and divide, count the digits. Add and subtract, count the decimals. 2.5 × 3.142 gives 7.9, two sig figs. 105.2 + 0.346 gives 105.5, one decimal place.

scenes.heading: Units
points: mL → L: divide by 1000 (250 mL = 0.250 L)
Convert units before using a formula
scenes.say: Convert units before you use a formula. To go from millilitres to litres, divide by a thousand. One atmosphere is one hundred and one point three two five kilopascals. Add two hundred and seventy-three to turn degrees Celsius into kelvin. If an answer is a thousand times off, check your millilitres.
scenes.caption: Convert units before you use a formula. mL to L: divide by 1000. 1 atm = 101.325 kPa. Add 273 to turn °C into K. If an answer is 1000 times off, check your mL.

points: Keep every digit, round once at the end
scenes.say: Quick recap. Leading zeros never count. Multiply and divide by sig figs, add and subtract by decimal places. Convert units first, and use the data book for constants. Keep every digit until the last line, then round once. Now try the practice questions!
